headline: Worries over AI spending sank Asian shares and pulled US bond yields to one-month lows, nudging the dollar lower. The Bank of Japan held rates but said inflation has reached its goal, and the yen firmed.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: A sell-off in AI-linked shares sent money into US Treasuries overnight, and the 10-year yield fell to about 4.9%, its lowest in over a month. That shrank the dollar's interest-rate edge, and the dollar index slipped below 102.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Since the US–Iran war began in February, high oil has kept US inflation well above the Federal Reserve's 2% goal, and the Fed raised rates in September. It held on Wednesday, and strong growth and inflation figures on Thursday kept a December hike likely. What changed: Big US tech companies' heavy spending on artificial intelligence spooked investors again: Alphabet, Google's owner, fell about 13% on Thursday, and Asian shares slid, with Japan's Nikkei down about 3%. Money moved into US government bonds, pulling the 10-year Treasury yield to about 4.9% and the 2-year to about 4.57%. The dollar index eased to about 101.8, though it is still set for a second monthly gain. What it means: This time a stock scare is weighing on the dollar rather than lifting it, because it pulls US yields down, and yields are what the dollar has been leaning on. Markets still see a December Fed hike as likely, so the dollar's floor depends on whether the share slide spreads or settles. The question to keep asking: are US yields falling because of fear, or because the Fed might not hike?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the US Employment Cost Index, a key wage gauge, at 7:30 AM CT (forecast 0.8% for the quarter), Chicago business activity at 8:45 AM, and Fed officials Mary Daly and Alberto Musalem at about 11:00 AM CT. October jobs figures come next week, after US clocks change on Sunday; the next Fed decision is December 9.

scenarios.bull: Wage costs jump or Fed speakers lean toward December; yields rebound and the index climbs back above 102.3.
scenarios.bear: The share slide deepens and pushes yields lower, or wages cool; the index falls below 101.4.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro edged up to about $1.120 as the US dollar softened, a day after touching its weakest since May 2025. Euro-area growth and October inflation figures come at 5:00 AM CT.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Energy costs from the Iran war have pushed euro-area inflation to about 3.8%, and the European Central Bank has raised its deposit rate twice this year, to 2.50%. On Thursday it held, and President Christine Lagarde said a hike had been discussed, which pointed markets to December. What changed: Nothing new from Europe overnight. The euro rose about 0.15% to near $1.1197 in Asia as lower US yields took some shine off the dollar. It is still headed for a fall of about 1% in October. What it means: The euro is being lifted by a softer dollar, not by its own news. Today's figures decide whether a December hike stays near-certain: hot inflation would lock it in and support the euro, while a weak reading would revive doubts at a time when growth is already flat and France's budget fight still weighs. The question to keep asking: does euro-area inflation stay hot enough to lock in December?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: French growth at 1:30 AM CT and German growth at 2:00 AM, euro-area growth for July to September and October inflation flash estimates at 5:00 AM (inflation was 3.8% in September), and German inflation at 8:00 AM CT. France's parliament votes on the revenue part of its budget on November 3.
numbers: ECB deposit rate 2.50%; December hike seen as very likely

scenarios.bull: Inflation runs above 3.8% and US wage figures cool; the euro rises above $1.125.
scenarios.bear: Inflation eases sharply or French bond worries return; the euro falls below $1.112.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: The pound rose to about $1.340 as the US dollar softened, and it is up about 1% in October. Markets still expect a Bank of England hike on November 5.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September, and markets see a Bank of England hike on November 5 as almost certain. Chancellor John Healey's first Budget on Wednesday passed calmly, and the pound hit its strongest against the euro since May 2025 on Thursday. What changed: No UK news overnight. The pound gained about 0.2% to near $1.340 as US bond yields fell and the dollar eased, shrugging off the slide in global shares. What it means: With the Budget behind it, the pound is trading on interest rates, and one of the most likely hikes among major banks keeps it near the top of the board. A deeper stock sell-off is the main risk, since the pound tends to suffer when investors turn cautious. The question to keep asking: does the Bank of England hint at a second hike in December?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Nationwide house prices at 2:00 AM CT and US wage figures at 7:30 AM CT, then the Bank of England decision at 6:00 AM CT on Thursday, November 5 (US clocks change on Sunday).

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: The Bank of Japan held its rate at 1.25%, but one board member voted for a hike and the bank said underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal. The yen firmed, with the dollar dipping to about ¥157.1, helped by falling US yields.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Japanese rates are far below US rates, which has kept the yen weak near ¥158 per dollar, and Tokyo has warned it is ready to step into the currency market. Most economists expect the Bank of Japan's next hike in December. What changed: The bank held by 8 votes to 1; Hajime Takata wanted a rise to 1.50%. Its quarterly outlook said underlying inflation is now broadly in line with the 2% goal, raised its price forecast for the year to March 2028 to 2.6% from 2.4%, and said risks to prices lean higher. Tokyo consumer prices, out just before, rose 2.8% from a year earlier, a touch above forecast. The dollar fell from about ¥157.8 to a low near ¥157.1, also pulled down by lower US yields and a rush into safe assets as Japanese shares fell about 3%. What it means: Saying inflation has reached its goal is the bank's strongest hint yet that it can keep raising rates, and markets put a December hike at about 80%. A higher Japanese rate would narrow the gap with the US that keeps the yen weak; a stock scare adds safety buying on top. The question to keep asking: how soon does the Bank of Japan raise rates again?
chapters.fx: What's next: Governor Kazuo Ueda's press conference began at 1:30 AM CT; how clearly he points to December decides whether the yen keeps its gains. Coming up: US wage figures at 7:30 AM CT. The next Bank of Japan decision is December 18.
numbers: Core price forecast for FY2027 raised to 2.6% (from 2.4%)

scenarios.bull: Ueda points clearly to December or shares keep falling; the dollar drops below ¥156.5.
scenarios.bear: Ueda sounds in no hurry and shares recover; the dollar climbs back above ¥158.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The franc rose to near a one-month high, about 0.821 per dollar, as the slide in AI-linked shares sent money looking for safety. There was no Swiss news behind it.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Swiss inflation is below target and the Swiss National Bank holds its rate at zero, so the franc mostly moves as a safe place for money in tense times. The bank has said it is less ready to fight a weaker franc. What changed: Heavy falls in Asian shares and lower US yields lifted the safe-haven currencies overnight. The dollar slipped about 0.6% to near 0.8214 francs, down from about 0.826 at Thursday's New York close. What it means: The franc is doing its usual job in a scare: drawing money when shares fall. With no rate rise in sight, its gains depend on how long the nerves last, and on whether trouble with Iran adds to them. The question to keep asking: are investors still looking for safety?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the KOF economic barometer at 3:00 AM CT (forecast 108.1) and US wage figures at 7:30 AM CT. Swiss inflation figures come next week; the next Swiss rate decision is December 10.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Aussie rose to about 70.4 US cents despite the slide in Asian shares, after Australian producer prices came in a little hotter than expected. A Reserve Bank of Australia hike on Tuesday is still the strong favourite.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Australian inflation has run above the Reserve Bank of Australia's forecasts, and the bank has raised rates four times this year. Hot consumer price figures on Wednesday made a fifth hike, on November 3, likely. What changed: Prices businesses charge each other rose 1.1% in July to September, slightly above the 1.0% forecast, and 3.6% from a year earlier. Private-sector borrowing grew 0.6% in September, a touch faster than expected. The Aussie gained about 0.2% to near 70.4 cents as the US dollar softened, even with share markets falling. What it means: Price pressure is still building further up the supply chain, which backs the case for a hike next week. That rate edge is holding the Aussie up even on a day when nervous markets usually hurt it. The question to keep asking: does anything talk the Reserve Bank of Australia out of November?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US wage figures at 7:30 AM CT, China's official factory surveys at 8:30 PM CT tonight, then the Reserve Bank of Australia decision at 9:30 PM CT on Monday, November 2 (after US clocks change).

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The loonie firmed to about 1.397 per US dollar as the US dollar softened and oil rose back above $116 a barrel. Canada's August growth figures come at 7:30 AM CT.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Higher energy prices pushed Canadian inflation up, and on Wednesday the Bank of Canada raised its rate to 2.50%, its first hike since 2023. Governor Tiff Macklem said more hikes are possible but the bank will move carefully. What changed: The US dollar eased to about 1.3966 loonies in Asia from about 1.399 at Thursday's close. Oil's rebound on reports of new US military options against Iran gave Canada, a big oil exporter, extra support. What it means: Canada's turn to hikes and costly oil both work for the loonie, though a deeper stock sell-off would test it. Markets give a December hike roughly even odds, so today's growth figures can move those odds either way. The question to keep asking: does Canadian data give the bank reason to hike again in December?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Canada's August GDP (forecast +0.2% on the month) and US wage figures, both at 7:30 AM CT. The next Bank of Canada decision is December 9.
numbers: Bank of Canada rate 2.50%; December hike ~45% priced

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The kiwi edged up to about 56.4 US cents as the US dollar softened. There was no New Zealand news; it is roughly flat for October.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: On Wednesday the Reserve Bank of New Zealand held its rate at 2.75% in a 4–3 vote when almost everyone expected a hike, and the kiwi fell sharply. The bank said more tightening is likely. What changed: Little. The kiwi rose slightly to near 56.4 cents in Asia, helped by lower US yields, while the slide in global shares kept gains small. What it means: The kiwi is waiting for New Zealand's own figures to show whether December's hike is firming up. Until then it follows the US dollar and the global mood, and nervous markets tend to cap it. The question to keep asking: does a December hike look more certain?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US wage figures at 7:30 AM CT and China's factory surveys at 8:30 PM CT tonight. New Zealand job figures come next week; the next Reserve Bank of New Zealand decision is December 9.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Oil rose about 1%, with Brent back near $116 a barrel, after a report that President Donald Trump was briefed on new military options against Iran. Brent is set for a gain of nearly 14% in October.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The US–Iran war, which began in February, has largely shut shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and kept oil above $100. US officials have warned allies to prepare for possible new strikes after the November 3 midterm elections. What changed: The Wall Street Journal reported that Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command, briefed Trump on options that include a return to major fighting. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said tankers hit their sea mines near Hormuz, which no one else has confirmed, and Yemen's Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi energy sites. US envoy Tom Barrack said the two sides were very close to a first deal, but Iran rejected the latest proposals. Brent rose to about $116.1 and US crude to about $103.3. What it means: Oil is swinging between deal hopes and fear of more fighting, and right now the fear has the upper hand. A higher barrel helps exporters like Canada and costs importers like Japan and the euro area. The question to keep asking: does the US move toward strikes or talks after the midterms?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the OPEC+ meeting on Sunday, expected to keep December output targets unchanged, then the US midterm elections on Tuesday, November 3, and any reply from Iran to US proposals.
numbers: Brent on track for ~14% gain in October

scenarios.bear: Iran agrees to formal talks; Brent falls below $111.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold slipped to about $3,996 an ounce in Asia, under $4,000, even as shares fell. Investors favoured US Treasuries for safety, and a likely December Fed hike keeps weighing on a metal that pays no interest.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Gold soared earlier in the Iran war but has struggled since the Fed resumed raising rates, because higher yields make a metal that pays nothing less attractive. It has been heading for a second monthly fall. What changed: Gold fell about 1% on Thursday to near $4,017 after strong US figures, then dipped below $4,000 in Asia. The share sell-off sent money into bonds rather than gold, and some investors may be selling gold to cover losses elsewhere. What it means: Lower US yields would normally help gold, but for now the Fed's hike path matters more. Central-bank buying and the risk of new US strikes on Iran give it some support below $4,000. The question to keep asking: does falling stock value turn into falling Fed hike odds?

calls.text: US bond rally on war fears: if the 10-year yield stays near 5.05% into the close, the yen holds its gains near ¥157; if yields rebound on the strong claims figure, the dollar climbs back toward ¥158
calls.note: Yields did not rebound; they fell further, to about 4.95%, on a tech sell-off, and the yen extended its gains to about ¥156.85.

calls.text: US 10-year yield below 5% after the tech sell-off: if Asian and European stocks keep falling overnight, the yen pushes toward ¥156 and the dollar index slips under 101.5; a rebound in stocks lifts yields and the dollar back toward ¥157.5
calls.note: Asian stocks kept falling (Nikkei −1.3%) and the dollar dipped to about ¥156.3, but steadied near ¥156.9 by 12:40 AM CT; the dollar index held at about 101.5 rather than slipping under it.

calls.text: Euro-area flash business surveys Fri 3:00 AM CT (manufacturing ~52.7, services ~52.6 expected), hours before Moody's on France: misses keep the euro near $1.12; beats firm December ECB hike bets and lift it
calls.note: The surveys missed (euro-area composite 51.9, France back in contraction at 48.4), and the euro stayed near $1.12.

calls.text: US flash PMIs Fri 8:45 AM CT (services ~58.0 expected) and Michigan inflation expectations 9:00 AM CT: firm readings lift yields back toward 5% and steady the dollar; soft ones extend the bond rally
calls.note: The surveys were firm on prices and the Michigan inflation outlook ticked up; the 10-year yield rose back to about 5.00% and the dollar index firmed to about 101.8 on Friday.

calls.text: SNB policy summary 2:30 AM CT: worry about a strong franc keeps December cut bets alive and caps the franc; a calmer tone lets it firm
calls.note: Calmer tone: the bank dropped its stronger readiness to intervene and gave no December cut signal. The franc firmed slightly, with the dollar near 0.823, and hit a three-month high against the euro.

calls.text: Saudi departure order: widening across the Gulf or a hit on Saudi output puts Brent well above $110 and lifts the dollar and loonie; staying contained lets oil drift
calls.note: Brent did climb well above $110 (about $113 by the close), but on reports of US–Israeli strike plans and Iranian tanker claims, not a wider departure order. The loonie edged up; the dollar slipped.

calls.text: UK retail sales Fri 1:00 AM CT (−0.2% expected): a strong print lifts December hike bets and the pound; a weak one trims both
calls.note: Sales fell 0.4%, worse than expected, yet the pound reached its strongest against the euro since May 2025 on Friday as a November Bank of England hike stayed near certain.

calls.text: US jobless claims Thu 7:30 AM CT (about 200,000 expected): staying low keeps the Fed's December hike near 90%; a jump trims it and weighs on the dollar
calls.note: Claims stayed low at 194,000 (200,000 expected), near their lowest in decades. December hike bets held near 90% (CME FedWatch, Oct 21); a sharp bond rally later still pulled the dollar lower.

calls.text: Moody's review of France Fri: a downgrade widens France's gap over German yields and weighs on the euro; holding the rating eases the pressure
calls.note: Moody's held France at Aa3; French yields eased on Monday and the euro led the majors in the European morning.

calls.text: Bailey 8:00 AM CT after the 3.5% UK inflation print: backing November without promising more keeps the pound near $1.34; any opening to a December follow-up lifts it; calling energy temporary trims it
calls.note: Neither branch: Bailey gave no new signal on rates. The pound still held near $1.34 (about 1.3395 at the New York close), with December's second hike about a coin toss.

calls.text: US crude oil stocks 9:30 AM CT (industry survey: about −4.9M barrels): a big official draw keeps Brent above $110; a build lets the rebound fade
calls.note: The draw came (−3.1M barrels, far more than forecast) and Brent briefly topped $110.8, but it still faded to $108.82 at the settle after the US Treasury's tanker licence and emergency fuel loans.

calls.text: Pakistan's mediation after Iran's uranium refusal: any confirmed opening drains oil's premium and lifts the euro and yen; more warships and no talks keep Brent near $110 into the close
calls.note: No opening: Rubio called a deal extremely difficult and more US warships headed in. Brent settled at $108.82, near $110 but off its high on Washington's supply moves rather than diplomacy.

calls.text: Japan national CPI Thu 6:30 PM CT (2.1% expected): a hot print keeps the BoJ's December hike near three in four; a soft one fades it and weighs on the yen
calls.note: Neither branch: 2.1% exactly as expected (1.7% prior), though the measure that also leaves out energy jumped to 2.4%. December hike pricing held near 80%.

calls.text: US–Iran framework: confirmation by either government drains oil's risk premium and pulls US long yields lower; another denial puts Brent back toward $110
calls.note: No confirmation from either government, and no fresh denial either. Brent still climbed back toward $110 overnight, on tanker attacks spreading to the Gulf of Oman rather than on the talks.

calls.text: RBA's Hauser 5:30 PM CT: leaning on sticky inflation keeps a November hike near 1 in 3; leaning on the softer job market trims it
calls.note: Hauser leaned on sticky inflation: the outlook is 'materially worse'. Odds of a November hike rose to about 40% from about 30%, and the Aussie hit a three-week high near 0.702.

calls.text: China Q3 GDP 4.5% vs 4.4% fc — the aussie's demand read
calls.note: Beat: 4.5% vs 4.4% fc (q/q 1.2%); retail +1.1% the standout. AUD/USD +0.3-0.5% to ~0.697, the night's best G10 performer; USD/CNH 6.6811, strongest since June 2022. Two-speed beat (factories lead, property -20.6% YTD).

calls.text: Petersburg Oil Terminal drone strike — Baltic supply risk into Monday's open vs the waiver's lower-price pull
calls.note: Fire CONFIRMED (Beglov; Fire Point confirmed its FP-1 hit the terminal); ~1 killed, several injured (figures vary); damage extent still unquantified. Crude's Sunday open came flat — neither the spike nor the tumble; Asia Brent -1.0 to -1.8%.

calls.text: Beirut strike fallout: the haven-bid tell at Monday's open
calls.note: No Hezbollah retaliation as of Monday's open (Qmati: strike crossed a 'red line', leadership to decide; IDF: normal routines). Haven bid stayed sheathed — DXY flat 101.80-101.83, havens ~flat in Asia. The tell held: no escalation, no haven extension.

calls.text: October FOMC priced as a hold (~85%) into the Saturday blackout; December is the live debate
Brent broke $108 on Ukraine refinery strikes — $105-112 range into the weekend (prior $104-108 call broken)
USD/CAD holds 1.41-1.43 into the BoC (Oct 28); Canada CPI Mon the trigger
calls.note: Oct 19: CPI passed without a break — USD/CAD ~1.411 at the NY close, still inside the range. Runs to the Oct 28 decision. Oct 20: dipped to ~1.409, a hair under the floor, as oil and BoC hike bets lifted the loonie. Oct 20 close: broke below the floor — USD/CAD ~1.406, strongest loonie since Sep 22, on BoC hike pricing (~80–85%) and Alberta's vote to remain.
The tripwire never bit — Friday's waiver suspends the duties outright with no end date. Superseded by the ~Dec 17 60-day review clock.
calls.text: Graham Act Oct-18 tripwire: waivers extended or enforcement begins — oil's Sunday open is the tell
Iran deal Sunday signing: Trump's 'OPEN TO ALL' vs Tehran's 'not tomorrow' — the strait itself is the verdict
calls.note: No signed deal carried by any major wire by 4pm CT Sunday; Trump's 'complete' claim stands unverified against Tehran's 'talks stalled'. Aggregator 'markets celebrate' content held — its futures numbers contradict Friday's verified settles. The signing test is claim day, not done day.

calls.text: Canada CPI Mon 7:30am CT (TD 3.2%, UBS 3.3%, RBC 3.0%): hot (3.3%+) revives the Oct 28 hike; soft (3.0%-) buries it to December
calls.note: Neither branch: 3.1% vs 3.2% expected, core measures cooled to 1.8–1.9%. October stayed about 1 in 4 (a hold), with about one quarter-point hike priced by December; consumers' inflation expectations rose to ~3.9% in the BoC survey. Correction (Oct 20): by Monday's close swaps had jumped to ~87% for an October hike on Macklem's Saturday forecast warning; the 1-in-4 figure was stale.

calls.text: UK CPI Wed 1am CT (3.4% fc vs 3.1%): 3.5%+ starts pricing a December follow-up; soft reopens Bailey's 2027 read
calls.note: Hot branch: 3.5% vs 3.4% expected (3.1% in August), the highest in 11 months. November's hike is near certain; how much December moved was not yet verified at write.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (ANZ 3.8% y/y): hot settles the RBNZ's two-way bet toward the hike side
calls.note: Not hot: inflation came in at 3.7%, a touch soft. The hike side still settled anyway, with October 28 now about 98% priced.

calls.text: Japan CPI Fri + BoJ Oct 29-30: Ueda's 'quite close' language tested — October hike stays ~25%
calls.note: Oct 19: swaps now put an October 30 hike under 5% (BBH), below the ~25% in the call. December ~80% unchanged. October hike odds fell to about 4%, far below the ~25% in the call; Japan's inflation came in at 2.1% as expected and December (~80%) is now the meeting that matters.

calls.text: France's revenue-section budget vote Tue: a clean pass narrows the French–German spread (~141bp); a defeat or big concessions widens it and weighs on the euro
calls.note: No vote on Tuesday: it was pushed to October 27, so neither branch played out.

calls.text: UK jobs Tue 1 AM CT (earnings ~3.8% expected): sticky pay firms the BoE hike case before Wednesday's inflation; cooling pay backs Bailey's calmer view
calls.note: Sticky side won: unemployment fell to 4.7% (4.9% expected) and regular pay rose 3.7% (3.6% expected); total pay and claims were softer. Pound +0.3% to ~1.334.

calls.text: Konarak follow-through: a US confirmation or more strikes keeps oil's supply premium and lifts US yields; silence lets the morning's waiver drop resume
calls.note: No confirmation (a US official denied the strike) and no new strike overnight, yet the premium held: Brent ~$109.8 Tuesday on low Gulf flows and Iran's Hormuz claims. The waiver-driven drop did not resume.

calls.text: BoC Oct 28 with ~87% priced for a hike: a hike is mostly in the loonie already; a hold would be the surprise and hit it
calls.note: The Bank of Canada hiked as priced, and the loonie barely moved on the day.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (~3.8% y/y): near forecast keeps the ~80% hike pricing; clearly soft reopens the hold and weighs on the kiwi
calls.note: Near forecast (3.7% vs 3.8%) and hike pricing held, rising to about 98%; the kiwi dipped only briefly.
